condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

Results attained under outcome 1 LASPNET (CSO) conducted advocacy for the passing of the National Legal Aid bill. Consensus building stakeholder engagements were held that composed of Members of Parliament, Legal Aid Service Providers These provided input into the draft National Legal Aid Bill. The Legal Aid Bill was presented to the 11th Parliament by a private mover for its 1st reading and referred to the Legal and Parliamentary Committee for further consultations. -Supported the National GBV/VAC COVID-19 response subcommittee to hold engagements with MDAs.
Outcome 2: National and sub-national systems and institutions plan, fund and deliver evidence-based programmes that prevent and respond to violence against women and girls and harmful practices, including in other sectors.
Results attained under Output indicator 2.1 - Result under Output indicator 2.1.1: Four (4) Ministries have developed and implemented programmes for prevention and response to VAWG. This include Ministry of Gender (Advocacy for GBV financing, capacity building), Ministry of Internal Affairs (border engagements on trafficking in persons), Ministry of Public Service (training and mentorship of government officials) and Ministry of Local Government (enhancing capacity of Local Council Courts on case management and response). - 7 District Local governments supported to develop Local Government GBV Action plans reflecting all related interventions in the districts for ease of coordination.
Output indicator 2.1.5 - Through the leadership of Ministry of Public Service, 2 pre and in-service training institutions included GBV modules in their programmes Nsamizi Training Institute for Social Development integrated GBV in 1 certificate course and 4 diploma courses. Uganda Management Institute integrated GVB in all Masters Programmes and 4 postgraduate diploma courses. This was complimented by TOTs conducted for 76 Males and 48 academic staff were in 3 pre-service and in-service training institutions. The experts will be supporting the trainings in the different institutions.
Output 2.1 Key officials at national and/or sub-national levels in all relevant institutions are better able to develop and deliver evidence-based programmes that prevent and respond to VAWG, especially for those groups of women and girls facing intersecting and multiple forms of discrimination, including in other sectors. Results attained under output 2.1: - Using the GBV e-course developed in phase one at Civil Service College of Uganda, 143 public 0ficials enrolled for the 1st Online training in GBV responsive planning and budgeting. So far, 71 Males and 19 males have graduated. Through the physical learning at the civil service college, 133 government officials (86 M: 47F) from MDAs and LGs attended face-to-face training on planning and budgeting for GBV mainstreaming. The trained officials have committed to forming GBV working groups, are continuing advocacy for increased gender financing and are supporting periodic monitoring of GBV indicators.
- As part of the Performance Management Circular, the Ministry of Public Service mentored 204 Males and 122 Females to increase performance management & internal accountability mechanisms for GBV response in these Local Governments. Support supervision was conducted in 34 Local Governments and 1 Regional Referral Hospital.
PSFU in collaboration with the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD) conducted on-hands training of 945 (M=415, F=530) artisanal miners on value addition in 3 districts of Kasese, Kitgum and Tororo. These gained appropriate skills to produce high quality products which are sold to enhance their incomes.
120 GBV survivor miners and out of school girls in Tororo and Kasese were given enterprise based skills in baking and tailoring, 140 women and out of school girls were given revolving grants to provide business start-up and boost ongoing business as livelihood enhancement tools. The beneficiaries were also sensitized on GBV prevention and response - Five (5) non-state institutions supported to develop strategies on ending VAWG. These included Private Sector Foundation Uganda on Gender Equality Seal, KAWOU on increasing male engagement and supporting artisanal miners in Amudat, COSMESS and HADS- supporting livelihood interventions for GBV survivors, Action Aid Uganda to support construction and operationalization of the GBV Shelters for GBV survivors in Amudat and Terego. MDA- Ministry of Local government developed a handbook for LCC that was used to build capacity on case management and response. - Ministry of Local Government built the capacity of 18 Local Council Courts (90 LCC Members (19 females and 71 males) in 18 Sub counties of Kitgum and Kyegegwa districts.The LCC practices enhanced include LCC procedures, alternative dispute resolution mechanisms, use of referral pathways for GBV issues and Adjudication of matters relating to i) the Domestic Violence Act, ii) the Children’s Act, and iii)Customary Land Matters. There is also improved LCC case recording and disposal, for instance, in Kitgum, out of the 438 cases registered, 40 cases were handled by the LCC while 289 took the matter to the court.
Contribution under Output 4.1: UNDP Support towards HIV/AIDS - UNDP supported capacity strengthening of capacity of Uganda AIDS Commission (UAC) in coordination, human rights and HIV programming. UAC was facilitated to convene human rights and HIV meetings amongst partners. The follow-on actions from the engagements informed some of the discussions at the 2022 National HIV symposium which was held on 8th – 10th November 2022. - UNDP supported UAC to assess the performance of government MDAs implementing large infrastructure projects in form of budget allocation (How much money they allocated to HIV mainstreaming in their work plans and budgets and budget performance. UNDP further supported re-orientation of MDAs in HIV mainstreaming (Ministry of Works and Transport, UNRA, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development. -UNDP contributed to system strengthening of civil society associations through human rights programming. -UNDP supported the strengthening of system of CSO association through creating a sustainable HIV financing environment. A study was undertaken on reflecting on funding gains and securing sustainability of programming in Key Population Organizations in Uganda. UNDP participated in the the study by KP organizations in partnership with Uganda AIDS commission. -UNDP strengthened capacity of the member companies of Private Sector Foundation. The One Dollar Initiative is a Private Sector- Led innovative domestic resource mobilization mechanism to eradicate HIV/AIDS and its associated health challenges in Uganda by 2030 – The initiative was supported to mobilize more companies into the initiative and to coordinate the existing ones. Enhanced the visibility to the One (1) Dollar Initiative at the National HIV symposium. -UNDP has routinely convened meetings that bring together UN Agencies on HIV and Human Rights to provide technical guidance to the nationals response. -UNDP contributed to the review of the National Equity Plan where UNDP is a member of the National Steering Committee. - UNDP provided technical guidance to the preparations for organizing the National HIV Symposium, World AIDS Day, Philly Luyaaya Day which are major advocacy days for in the HIV response, where Uganda as a country reviews gains made in the response and sets an agenda for the subsequent year.

description.narrative:
This Indicator measures the number of policies on ending VAWG drafted/ strengthened. Strengthened means revision of policies or guidelines to expand their scope or align with international standards.
Note: The value for this indicator is only is counted if the revised or newly developed law is passed by parliament or policy is approved by government with evidence of date of approval or when passed.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of Highest-level mechanisms housed at either President, Vice-President, or Prime Minister Office with connected coordination mechanisms formed at sub-national level after the single national mechanism is established. Relevant stakeholders mean that the mechanism include staff from different sectors and representation from marginalized groups (e.g. PWDs, Eldery,non-nationals including refugees, Youths, Children, IDPs, miniority groups etc) Clear mandate implies the mechanism has clear mission and unifying statements."
